core_obligations: Translate to a representation (proof lines 10424-10436): choosing a geometric point sbar of the connected scheme S, the sheaf F corresponds to a finite dimensional F_l-vector space M with continuous action of the fundamental group, and the author examines the action of a suitable finite quotient.

Choose the covering (proof lines 10436-10448): using the existence of a finite etale covering trivialising F, the author restricts to a finite quotient of the fundamental group of order prime to l and produces a finite etale morphism f : T -> S of degree prime to l.

Produce the filtration (proof lines 10448-10457): over T the representation becomes a module over the group algebra of a finite group of order prime to l, which is a product of matrix algebras over F_l, so the module admits a filtration with quotients Z/l, giving the stated filtration of f^{-1}F.
proof_roadmap: Turn the problem into a statement about a finite dimensional F_l-representation of a finite quotient of the fundamental group.
Choose a finite etale covering of degree prime to l realising that quotient.
Over that covering, use the structure of the group algebra in characteristic l to filter the module with trivial successive quotients.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite type locally constant sheaf of F_l-vector spaces on a connected scheme becomes, after a finite etale cover of degree prime to l, a sheaf admitting a finite filtration with successive quotients the constant sheaf Z/l (statement lines 10413-10422). The proof translates the sheaf into a finite dimensional F_l-representation of a finite quotient of the fundamental group of order prime to l (proof lines 10424-10436), realises that quotient by a finite etale covering of the required degree (proof lines 10436-10448), and then uses the structure of the group algebra of a finite group of order prime to l to produce the filtration (proof lines 10448-10457). The non-formal content is the use of the order-prime-to-l hypothesis through the group algebra. The claim is H2: one translation plus one linear-algebra argument over F_l.
